cells.tense: The work has been carried through to its end, and the person is here in it, satisfied without needing it to be perfect.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you actually finished, not what is coming next. Let that naming be the whole point of the conversation. It keeps the appetite for more honest, fed from what is already in your hands.
cells.core:
A finished thing sits on the shelf and you can look at it without grabbing the next one. What got made arrived, the loose edges are part of it, and you are still in the room where it happened instead of already turned toward the door. That staying is the making, not a pause in it. The satisfaction you get is not because everything came out clean; it is because what you imagined got felt all the way through.

The appetite for the next thing is still there, and it can grow from what you are holding rather than from pushing harder at what is not done. Say out loud, to somebody who watched it happen, one real thing you finished. Let the sentence stay short and let it be the point.

cells.verb: feeling what was imagined all the way through to its fullest end

cells.tense: A thing was completed some time back, and the person is hovering at the threshold, not yet living on the other side of it.
cells.ask: Write one sentence on paper about how something you already completed actually turned out, not how it was meant to. Read it back once. Direction comes from what the sentence shows, not from pushing at the bare spot where nothing has landed yet.
cells.core: A completed thing sits somewhere you can still see it, and the account of it can be spoken plainly — the part that worked, the part that did not, the part that surprised you — and the saying is what lets the next thing start on its own. The account is missing. You can recognize how the thing landed, better than the one you give anyone, and that recognition has no outlet, so no day gets to be the day it is finished and nothing sets out toward what is next. The doorway behind is open, and you are facing it instead of walking through. One sentence on paper tells you more than another push will.

cells.tense: The pen is down while the record keeps getting written: endings keep happening in the person's own hands and get described as if they happened by themselves.
cells.ask: Point to one thing you finished recently and say plainly that you finished it, with no thanks to timing or circumstance. Refining what matters next gets quieter once the claim is on the table.
cells.core: A finished thing sits where you left it, and pointing at it and saying what you did — the working, the waiting, the part where it nearly came apart — is not pride; it is a plain record, and it keeps the next decision clean because you know what the last one actually cost. What happens instead is that the endings get filed under timing, or the situation, or luck, or a group that happened to pull it off. The pen was in your hand the whole time. Naming it does not inflate anything, it just puts the claim where the work has been all along, and that is what lets you see what matters next.
